mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT keep falling while RESIDENTIAL keeps rising, fewer in-person trips and commutes will suppress discretionary stops, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not stay below its prior 4-week mean over the next 28 days despite continued declines in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT and a higher RESIDENTIAL level.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp weekly drop in TRANSIT below its recent trajectory marks immediate avoidance of shared travel, which reduces same-week retail visits and drags RETAIL_REC down within one to two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to weaken within 7 to 14 days after a week-on-week TRANSIT decline larger than 8 points.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both remain depressed at the same time, the city is likely under broader activity suppression, and retail-and-recreation mobility should continue to fall over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES below -30 and TRANSIT below -50 simultaneously
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next 28 days when both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT stay below the stated thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in RESIDENTIAL paired with weaker WORKPLACES means more time spent at home and fewer discretionary outings, so retail-and-recreation mobility should stay below the recent 4-week average over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last 4-week mean over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated and WORKPLACES remain subdued.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in PARKS mobility signals colder or less favorable outdoor conditions, which shifts leisure away from shopping and recreation districts and lowers RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -15 and stays there for 2 weekly means
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall within 14 days after PARKS remains below -15 for two consecutive weekly means.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM becomes less negative while RETAIL_REC keeps falling, households are reallocating trips toward essentials and away from discretionary shopping, implying further weakness in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM improves by at least 5 points while RETAIL_REC stays below -40
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rebounds over the next 28 days even though GROCERY_PHARM improves by at least 5 points from a deeply negative level.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, any upward move in TRANSIT is a leading sign that mobility controls are easing, and retail-and-recreation visits should begin recovering within one to two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 14 days after TRANSIT turns upward from its recent low in a reopening regime.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM both fall together, leisure and errand activity are both weakening, which should translate into a faster decline in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM both decline week-on-week for 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not become more negative over the next 28 days after two consecutive weekly declines in both PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM.
